card.text: Earth's only natural satellite, always turning the same face toward us.

introduction.text: The Moon likely formed after a Mars-sized body collided with Earth. Its dark maria are old impact basins filled with lava.

surface.title: LROC photographic mosaic
surface.summary: LRO photographs from 2009–2011; crater shadows are part of the images.

midnight-temperature.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: midnight temperature
midnight-temperature.summary: Midnight temperatures fitted from Diviner data, 2009–2022, within 70° of the equator. They average many nights.

heat-anomalies.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: heat anomalies
heat-anomalies.summary: Midnight warmth (red) or coolness (blue) compared with typical lunar soil. Warm spots are not signs of internal heat.

rock-abundance.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: rock abundance
rock-abundance.summary: The share of ground covered by rocks, modeled from Diviner midnight data. It estimates area, not boulder counts.

topography.title: LOLA LDEM16 elevation model
topography.summary: Height above or below a 1,737.4 km sphere, from LRO's laser altimeter. Shading shows slopes.

crust.title: Crustal-thickness model
crust.summary: Thickness inferred from gravity and topography. It depends on assumed rock densities.

silicate-signature.title: Diviner Christiansen feature, 2009–2016
silicate-signature.summary: An infrared emissivity peak between 8.0 and 8.5 µm that tracks silicate composition, not mineral amounts.

geology.title: USGS unified global geology (2020 v2)
geology.summary: Geologic units and their relative ages from the 2020 USGS map. Colors are map units, not surface color.
